title: SIU investigating fatal police shooting in Peterborough
subtitle: Billy Shea, 27, who died after he was shot Tuesday night, was wanted by police on 2 warrants
article: Ontario's police watchdog is investigating after an officer fatally shot a 27-year-old man in Peterborough Tuesday night.
With permission from family, the Special Investigations Unit identified the victim as Billy Shea.
Peterborough police say they saw a stolen car in Millbrook around 8:35 p.m. and started following the vehicle.
Shea, who police say was wanted on two outstanding warrants, was driving the car on Highway 115, according to preliminary information released by the SIU.
Shortly after, the vehicle was in a collision with another civilian vehicle around Highway 115 and The Parkway in Peterborough, the SIU said.
Police officers approached the scene and "began negotiations with Mr. Shea," said Monica Hudon, spokesperson for the SIU.
One officer fired his weapon around 9:40 p.m. and Shea was hit, she said.
Shea was brought to hospital, where he was pronounced dead. A post-mortem is scheduled for Thursday morning.
Hudon said the vehicle was "of interest" to police because it was believed to have been involved in a number of robberies in the Barrie area.
"Understanding what transpired - including whether or not Mr. Shea was armed - is part of the SIU's investigation," Hudon said in an email.
OPP Detective Const. Steve Sermet confirmed that Billy Shea is the same man wanted on a Canada-wide warrant in May for breaching statutory release and not returning to a halfway house.
Shea was serving a five year sentence for multiple counts of robbery and vehicle theft, according to the OPP.
He was also the subject of a second warrant in July for robbery with a gun, issued by Hamilton Police. Police had not found Shea between the two warrants. He had been released on March 22, 2019.
Police previously said Shea was known to frequent Hamilton, Stoney Creek, Burlington and the Niagara Region.

Cassie Wildman was driving home around 8:30 p.m. Tuesday when she saw a red Mustang "flying" off the Highway 115 off-ramp and over the median. The car was coming straight at her vehicle, she said, with a police car on his tail.
Wildman said she swerved to avoid him, before the red car hit the vehicle behind her, creating a "big explosion of debris."
By the time she turned around, Wildman said she saw a police officer with a gun pointed at the Mustang. She immediately told her son to get his phone.
When she looked again, Wildman said she saw multiple people with guns drawn.
Witness video shows standoff between man and police in Peterborough
"Very scary," she said. "When you start seeing guns drawn ... the situation becomes very amplified."
Officers told her the standoff was still happening about a half hour later, when she came back to talk to police.
The SIU has assigned six investigators and three forensic investigators to the incident.

There is one subject officer from the Peterborough Police Service. A subject officer is a police officer whose conduct appears to have caused the death or serious injury under investigation, according to the SIU.

Additionally, five officers with the Ontario Provincial Police and seven officers with Peterborough police have been designated as witness officers. A witness officer is a police officer who is involved in the incident under investigation but is not a subject officer.
The SIU is asking anyone with information to contact the lead investigator at 1-800-787-8529.
Anyone with video is asked to upload it through the SIU website.
All ramps leading to the Parkway from Highway 115 were closed for the investigation, said Peterborough Police.
Peterborough police would not confirm if any officers have been suspended, as it is an SIU investigation.
The SIU is an arm's-length agency that investigates reports involving police where there has been death, serious injury or allegations of sexual assault.
